# English: 5,000 people can ride on the shell of Gigantamax Lapras for a very comfortable ride without any issues. Lapras can use its giant ring to break any icebergs that may prevent it from swimming.
A Ghost Pokemon whose body is 95% poisonous gas. Because it is mostly gas, Gastly will dwindle away when exposed to strong winds.

A Legendary Pokemon resembling a tortoise and a ram. Because of its intense body heat, certain parts of its body are melted slightly out of shape. Boiling blood, like magma, circulates through its body.

A Legendary Pokemon that resembles a serpent. This form of Zygarde is thought to monitor those who destroy the ecosystem from deep with its cave. Should the regions ecosystem fall into disarray, it will appear and reveal its power.
A Legendary Pokemon thats a relatively small canine. 10% Forme has razor-sharp teeth and can reach speeds up to 100 km/h (60 mph).
A Mega Evolution of Abomasnow. The sprouts on its back have grown into great shafts of ice.
A Mega Evolution of Absol. Its fur is longer overall, and the increased energy coursing through its body makes the fur at the back of its mane stand on end, so that it appears to have wings.

A Mega Evolution of Aerodactyl. When it Mega Evolves, Mega Aerodactyl becomes even more vicious than it was before. The reason for that supposedly is because of the excess of this Pokemon's power is causing it pain.
A Mega Evolution of Aggron. Using its horns, it is said to be able to destroy a steel tank.
A Mega Evolution of Alakazam. The organ on its forehead is said to emit psychic power.
A Mega Evolution of Altaria. Mega Altaria's singing voice is even more beautiful than that of its regular form. It is known for its sociable personality and is not timid.
A Mega Evolution of Ampharos. The orb on its tail can shine so bright, that it can be seen from space. People have used the light as a beacon, or to send signals across the ocean.
A Mega Evolution of Audino. Mega Audino can release pulses that reduce hostility, and the secondary feelers can put those who come in contact with them into a deep sleep.
A Mega Evolution of Banette. As Mega Banette, this Pokemon gains several additional zippers, revealing parts of Mega Banette's body.
A Mega Evolution of Beedrill. Fast-acting poison is stored in the stingers on its limbs, while the tail stinger produces a slow-acting poison that is used to finish opponents.

A Mega Evolution of Blastoise. The two cannons on its back are replaced by a single, central water cannon of greater size. This cannon extends forward over Mega Blastoise's head and is said to have a blast range of over 6 miles (10 km).
A Mega Evolution of Blaziken. As it unleashes a flurry of savage kicks, its legs can begin to burn from the friction of the surrounding atmosphere.

A Mega Evolution of Camerupt. It has a deep hatred of water or any moisture, and has an explosive personality and a short temper. The volcano on its back erupts constantly in an effort to intimidate its foes.
A Mega Evolution of Charizard. Mega Charizard X breathes blue flames out the sides of its mouth, and the flame on its tail now burns blue with increased heat.
A Mega Evolution of Charizard. Mega Charizard Y is said to have incredible flying prowess, being able to reach incredible heights.
A Mega Evolution of Diancie. Because of its noble beauty, Mega Diancie is commonly referred to as "the Royal Pink Princess".
A Mega Evolution of Gallade. When the situation demands, Mega Gallade can use its psychic power to reshape both arms into blades simultaneously, and fight using a dual-wielding style.
A Mega Evolution of Garchomp. The claws and fins on its arms morph together to form sharp blades.

A Mega Evolution of Gardevoir. There are two horns in the center of its chest, extending to either side. These horns are said to be a physical manifestation of this Pokemon's heart, and it is able to use tremendous psychic power now that it is open.
A Mega Evolution of Gengar. A third eye appears on its forehead. This new unblinking eye allows it to see into other dimensions.
A Mega Evolution of Glalie. The horns on top Mega Glalie's head have been partially turned into ice, with the addition of a third horn on its forehead.
A Mega Evolution of Gyarados. Huge and vicious, it is capable of destroying entire cities in a rage.
A Mega Evolution of Heracross. This Pokemon has a high body temperature, so it opens the shell on its torso to allow heat to escape.
A Mega Evolution of Houndoom. Due to the greater heat that it can produce, its claws exhibit a more intense red color.

A Mega Evolution of Kangaskhan. The mother's happiness over its child's growth is the source of its additional strength. However, it feels uneasy about the child's future, as it is only skilled at fighting and nothing else.
A Mega Evolution of Latias. Its body can refract light, which allows it to become invisible or alter its appearance.
A Mega Evolution of Latios. Its body can refract light, which allows it to become invisible or alter its appearance.
A Mega Evolution of Lopunny. A full-power strike from Mega Lopunny's ears can crumple steel plates.
A Mega Evolution of Manectric. The mane on Mega Manectric is considerably larger than its previous state.
A Mega Evolution of Mawile. Mega Mawile has a second set of jaws protruding from the back of its head. It is also able to control each jaw independently of each other.

A Mega Evolution of Medicham. Using its enhanced willpower, Mega Medicham has formed four ghost-like arms around itself. The more trained its spirit, the more realistic and dexterous its self-created arms become.
A Mega Evolution of Metagross. Its multiple brains process information simultaneously, enabling it to calmly assess the tide of a battle and defeat its opponent with accuracy.

A Mega Evolution of Pidgeot. The crest is sensitive to air currents, acting like a large antenna and stabilizing Mega Pidgeot's flight. Additionally, its increased wing power allows it to produce gust capable of destroying huge trees.

A Mega Evolution of Pinsir. When it Mega Evolves, Pinsir is left in a constant state of excitement. Mega Pinsir can travel up to 30 mph (48 kph) and uses its two large horns to pierce its enemies before shredding them.

A Mega Evolution of Rayquaza. Inside Rayquaza's body lies an organ that contains the same power as a Mega Stone. By consuming meteoroids as it flies through the stratosphere, the mikado organ will be filled with enough energy to enable Rayquaza's Mega Evolution.

A Mega Evolution of Sableye. All the energy from its Mega Evolution is concentrated into the red jewel on its chest, causing it to detach from Sableyes body and significantly increase in size. The enlarged jewel is said to boast such incredible hardness that no attack can even leave a scratch on it.

A Mega Evolution of Salamence. As a result of its Mega Evolution, Salamence becomes even more brutal than ever before, to the point where it is liable to turn against the Trainer who raised it. Because of this, Mega Salamence is feared as "the blood-soaked crescent".
A Mega Evolution of Sceptile. Mega Sceptile can cut off a portion of its tail to fire it like a missile at an opponent.
A Mega Evolution of Scizor. The barbs on Mega Scizor's claws can stab through concrete, and opponents caught in them are unable to escape.
A Mega Evolution of Sharpedo. With explosive propulsion, it can exceed 125mph (201kph) in an instant.
A Mega Evolution of Slowbro. Mega Slowbro's energy has gathered into Shellder, which has increased its hardness. This allows it to act as an armor so hard that nothing can scratch it.
A Mega Evolution of Steelix. The cells within its body, crystallized by the energy produced from Mega Evolution, are stronger than any mineral and able to withstand any temperature.
A Mega Evolution of Swampert. Mega Swampert fills the organs on its back with air before diving underwater or battling. It uses that pressure to increase the power of its punch.
A Mega Evolution of Tyranitar. The scales on Mega Tyranitar's belly seethe with energy, enabling it to emanate more power.
A Mega Evolution of Venusaur. Venusaur uses its flower to catch the suns rays to convert them into energy, which causes the flower to take on colors that are more vibrant.
A Mega evolution of Lucario. Mega Lucario was originally believed to be the first discovered Mega Evolution.
A Pokemon based on a cicadas shed exoskeleton. It is said that looking into the crack on its back will steal ones spirit.

A Pokemon composed of an oblong, irregularly-shaped clay slab. Runerigus was formed from a painting imbued with an ancient curse, which was activated by absorbing the spirit of a Yamask and brought the painting to life.

A Pokemon composed of rock salt. Nacli are born deep within the earth, inside layers of rock salt. Bits of salt are scraped off of Nacli as it travels the ground, although Nacli is able to create and replenish the salt inside its body.

A Pokemon composed of seven symbiotic partners known as "syrpents" living within an apple made of red syrup. The syrpents that form Hydrapple have inconstant temperaments. On the rare occasion that the syrpents' moods align, Hydrapple reaches its full potential.

A Pokemon consisting of two spherical heads connected by a thin tube. Each of Weezing's heads contains a different toxin. It mixes its gases by inflating one head and deflating the other. When its gases mix, Weezing becomes more toxic and putrid.

A Pokemon consisting of two spherical heads connected by a thin tube. Galarian Weezing consumes particles from the polluted air. It expels clean air instead of droppings. The toxins within Weezing's body are accumulated into poison gas clouds that leaks and drifts around it.

A Pokemon covered in vines. Tangela can ensnare and entangle anything that moves too close to it with its vines. The vines constantly jiggle and sway, unnerving enemies and deterring herbivores that might mistake Tangela for a shrub.

A Pokemon encased inside a thick shell made of rock. While its arms and legs are developing inside the shell, Pupitar is capable of venting gas to propel itself around, and can generate enough force to knock down mountains.

A Pokemon formed from sand. Sandygast is born from grudges that seep into the sand, such as from Pokemon that suffer defeat in battle. It can suck the life force of people or Pokemon through its mouth.
A Pokemon in the shape of a sarcophagus. Ancient legends once told Cofagrigus could eat nearby humans and turn their lifeless bodies into mummies.
A Pokemon in the shape of an eye. Motionless as if dead, its body is faintly warm to the touch. People think this Pokemon may come from another world.
A Pokemon made completely out of programming code. Due to its man-made origins, Porygon does not need to breathe or eat, though it can still accept food if given.
A Pokemon made of matcha tea. It pretends to be tea in order to trick people into drinking it, so it can absorb their life force.

A Pokemon made of matcha tea. It pretends to be tea in order to trick people into drinking it, so it can absorb their life force. It lives inside a superb teacup that was crafted by a potter of great renown.

A Pokemon made up of an anchor and ship wheel, held together by a mass of seaweed. The soul of seaweed adrift in the waves became reborn as this Pokemon. It maintains itself with new infusions of seabed detritus and seaweed.
A Pokemon resembling a Venus flytrap. With its mouth wide open, it attracts the prey it waits for with a sweet-smelling saliva, then chomps down.
A Pokemon resembling a balloon. It has been known to steal children that mistake it for a regular balloon. However, due to its light weight, it can be resisted easily and is often pulled around.

A Pokemon resembling a barracuda. Should Arrokuda see any movement near it, it will charge in a straight line using its sharp pointed jaws, though its movements tend to become sluggish when it eats too much, which is typically when Cramorant appear to swallow it up.
A Pokemon resembling a bear or panda cub. Despite its small size, Stufful has extraordinary strength and can knock out even well trained Pokemon if they are unprepared.

A Pokemon resembling a bear. While Bewear may appear friendly, it is actually a very dangerous Pokemon. It must never be approached carelessly, even if it is merely swinging its arms around in a friendly fashion.
A Pokemon resembling a blimp. Drifblim is strong enough to lift Pokemon or people, but has no control over its flight. This causes it to drift with the wind and end up anywhere.
A Pokemon resembling a chrysalis. Metapod generally remains motionless, preparing its soft innards for evolution inside its hard shell.

A Pokemon resembling a cormorant. Cramorant is a gluttonous Pokemon that can swallow other Pokemon whole. Its preferred prey are Arrokuda, but sometimes it swallows other Pokemon such as Pikachu, attempting to spit them out if they realise their mistake.
A Pokemon resembling a durian. It can stick its spikes into cave walls to absorb the minerals from the rocks. If threatened, it can shoot a barrage of spikes so it can escape by rolling away.
A Pokemon resembling a flattened durian. It can use its spiked appendages to either cling to ceilings of its cave or walk around. When hanging, it can attack its prey underneath by shooting spikes.
A Pokemon resembling a gamebird. Female Unfezant are more adept at flying than male Unfezant.
A Pokemon resembling a gamebird. Male Unfezant threaten their opponents by swinging their heads.
A Pokemon resembling a manta ray. Mantyke is a friendly Pokemon that can be found swimming near the oceans surface with schools of Remoraid.

A Pokemon resembling a powerfully built lemur with broad shoulders. This Pokemon's battle strategy involves throwing Berries at opponents, hard ones for damage and soft ones to obscure vision, and confusing opponents by throwing the Berry to other troop members.
A Pokemon resembling a robotic bird. A mysterious life-form resembling Delibird. It possesses a spherical apparatus from which can fire huge blasts of ice to propel itself through snowy lands.
A Pokemon resembling a salamander or lizard. Salazzle is a female-only species. It creates a reverse harem with the male Salandit it lives with.

A Pokemon resembling a sand castle. Palossand controls adults to make them build it a sand castle, which provides it a disguise and defense. However, Palossand is able to replenish any sand it loses on its own.
A Pokemon resembling a scoop of vanilla ice cream. It creates ice inside its body by drinking water, and expels it to hide itself or freeze opponents.

A Pokemon resembling a small olive tree. Arboliva has a calm and compassionate nature, kind enough to share its nutrient-rich, aromatic oil with weakened Pokemon. However, when threatened, it will drive back enemies by launching its oil at them, with a force powerful enough to destroy a boulder.

A Pokemon resembling a small snake. Silicobra collects sand by swallowing it and is able to shoot it from its nostrils, an ability it uses to blind predators so it can escape by burrowing into the ground.
A Pokemon resembling a spider. It delivers headbutts with the water bubble on its head. Small Pokemon get sucked into the bubble, where they drown.
A Pokemon resembling a spider. The bubble serves as a means of protection to Dewpider's soft head and allows it to breathe when on land.
A Pokemon resembling a starfish. Those attacked by Toxapexs poison will suffer great pain for three days and three nights. Even after recovering, there will be some aftereffects.

A Pokemon resembling a swirled scoop of vanilla ice cream. Vanillite can blow winds as low as -58 F (-50 C) (9910 U), which causes it to create ice crystals and make it snow in nearby areas when it exhales.
A Pokemon resembling a weasel and a sea otter. Its tail acts as a boat propeller by spinning, though it was seen flying using its tail.
A Pokemon resembling an anthropomorphic otter or weasel. To help it dive, Floatzel can deflate its floatation sac, and then inflate it once again when it wishes to surface.
A Pokemon resembling an insect or crustacean. It is very strong, to the point that it can carry heavy rocks for a long time, even through arid lands where it resides.

A Pokemon resembling six light pink eggs, usually seen arranged with five heads huddled around a sixth. The heads communicate with each other by using a form of telepathy that only they can understand.

A Pokemon said to be created when a lonely spirit possesses a cold, leftover cup of tea. The teacup in which this Pokemon makes its home is a famous piece of antique tableware. Many forgeries are in circulation.
A Pokemon said to be created when a lonely spirit possesses a cold, leftover cup of tea. The teacup in which this Pok├⌐mon makes its home is a famous piece of antique tableware.
A Pokemon seemingly formed out of stone. The armored plates on its lower jaw are stronger than steel, and allow Hisuian Avalugg to break through boulders easily and shovel through deep snow.
A Pokemon shaped like a lawnmower. Rotom has the ability to enter and control appliances and will often pull pranks on unsuspecting people.
A Pokemon shaped like a microwave oven. Rotom has the ability to enter and control appliances and will often pull pranks on unsuspecting people.
A Pokemon shaped like a refrigerator. Rotom has the ability to enter and control appliances and will often pull pranks on unsuspecting people.
A Pokemon shaped like a washing machine. Rotom has the ability to enter and control appliances and will often pull pranks on unsuspecting people.
A Pokemon shaped like an electric fan. Rotom has the ability to enter and control appliances and will often pull pranks on unsuspecting people.
A Pokemon similar to a koala. This Pokemon has never been seen awake. While its expression sometimes changes as if it is aware of its surroundings, this appears to be a result of its dreams instead.

A Pokemon similar to a red ladybug. Ledyba secretes an aromatic fluid from where its legs join its body, which it uses to communicate with other Ledyba. Ledyba conveys its feelings to other Ledyba by altering the fluids scent.
A Pokemon somewhat resembling a cyclops. The antenna on Dusknoir's head allows it to receive transmissions from the spirit world, which tell it to bring people there.

A Pokemon surrounded by a blob of translucent, gelatinous substance. Reuniclus controls its powerful arms using psychic powers. It can form a network with the brains of other Reuniclus by clasping hands with them.

A Pokemon surrounded by a gel-like substance. It has two brains, which occasionally causes it to attempt two different actions at once. However, its exhibits greater psychic powers when the brains think alike.
A Pokemon that appears like a legless lump. Its favorite food is a type of mushroom that grows beneath dead grass, though it also eats Berries.

A Pokemon that bears a strong resemblance to a ferret. Its most notable feature is its long skinny body, which is used for slipping through the small entrances to its nest and squirm through small spaces to escape foes.
A Pokemon that bears similarity to an owl. It has exceptional hearing and eyesight, can fly silently, and can turn its heads at a 180 angle to increase its intellect.

A Pokemon that has the appearance of a pile of trash spilling out of a large, torn garbage bag. Garbodor is able to spray poisonous gas and filth from its fingertips, but only from its right hand. It also finishes off opponents by subduing them with its left arm and spewing an awful-smelling toxic gas from its mouth.

A Pokemon that is comprised of a golden sword and ornate shield. It is said to be able to detect the innate qualities of leadership; legend has it that whoever Aegislash recognizes as a worthy leader is destined to become king.
A Pokemon that is heavily based on the coelacanth. Relicanth is a filter feeder, and it feeds on microscopic organisms with its toothless mouth.

A Pokemon that is similar to a mushroom. Toedscool has two long, thin, white legs resembling tentacles or mycelium, which it uses to run at a speed of 30 mph (50 km/h). Although Toedscool physically resembles Tentacool, the two species are biologically unrelated.
A Pokemon that looks like a stylized personification of the Grim Reaper. It is said that this Pokemon will spirit away disobedient children, and it has been described to enjoy the crying of children.
A Pokemon that looks similar to a tree. Sudowoodo disguises itself as a tree and stands along paths to avoid being attacked.

A Pokemon that resembles a baby vulture. It seems to be wearing a broken skull as a diaper-like undergarment, hence its species name. Vullaby either finds this bone itself or uses one found for it by Mandibuzz.
A Pokemon that resembles a bipedal crocodile. Totodile tends to be playful by nature, and has a habit of biting anything it sees, including its Trainer.
A Pokemon that resembles a bipedal sea turtle. Carracosta has extremely strong jaws and have enough power in its slap to open a hole in the bottom of a tanker.

A Pokemon that resembles a bipedal wasp. Disturbing a swarm of Beedrill will cause the whole colony to attack. It flies at high speed and attacks using the large venomous stingers on its forelegs and abdomen.
A Pokemon that resembles a blob with stubby arms and legs. Its body is soft and rubbery, allowing it to inflate by inhaling. While it is inflated, it is able to move by bouncing or floating.

A Pokemon that resembles a box jellyfish. Tentacool absorbs sunlight and refracts it using water inside its body to convert it into beam energy. It is also able to control Pokemon it touches with its tentacles.
A Pokemon that resembles a bull. It causes vegetation to grow, and then it absorbs energy from the growth.
A Pokemon that resembles a caterpillar. Caterpie will shed its skin many times before finally cocooning itself in thick silk.
A Pokemon that resembles a cross between a salamander and a hippopotamus. Galarian Slowpoke are known to relax on seashores and riverbanks without a care in the world.

A Pokemon that resembles a cross between a salamander and a hippopotamus. Slowpoke has notoriously dim intellect, and often forgets what it was doing. It takes a long time to respond to outside stimuli.

A Pokemon that resembles a duck or bipedal platypus. Psyduck is constantly stunned by its headache and is unable to think very clearly. It usually stands immobile, trying to calm its headache. However, when its headache becomes too severe, it releases tension in the form of strong psychic powers.
A Pokemon that resembles a duck. Farfetch'd is always seen carrying a leek stalk or spring onion. Unable to live without its stick, Farfetch'd will defend the stalk with its life.
A Pokemon that resembles a duck. Its body has developed a much stronger frame that gives it the strength required to carry its leek. However, the sheer mass of it makes it hard for Farfetch'd to fly.
A Pokemon that resembles a full garbage bag. Trubbish emits noxious, burp-like gases which, when inhaled, will render the victim bedridden for a week.

A Pokemon that resembles a giant chain of boulders that become smaller towards the tail. This Pokemon has a magnet in its brain that serves as an internal compass. Its body absorbs many hard objects, making its body very solid.

A Pokemon that resembles a giant chain of boulders that become smaller towards the tail. This Pokemon has a magnet in its brain that serves as an internal compass. This is a special Onix with a body made out of crystal glass.
A Pokemon that resembles a lantern. Lampent can sense when someone is about to die, whom it visits and steals the spirit from the person's body.

A Pokemon that resembles a massive goliath with a body of coal atop of it. In battle, the coal on its head will burn bright red and radiate heat that sends sparks flying, scorching their surroundings.
A Pokemon that resembles a minecart. Carkol forms coal inside of its body and frequently drops said coal.
A Pokemon that resembles a modestly sized rock. When its shell breaks, Minior becomes lighter and capable of attacking quickly, but it cannot survive for long with its core exposed.

A Pokemon that resembles a plant bulb with a round body. Oddish will wander up to 1000 feet (300 meters) during the night to scatter its seeds and find a nutrient-rich patch of soil in which to plant itself.
A Pokemon that resembles a quadruped wolf. In order to avoid needless fighting, the Midday Form prefers to live alone and does not form a pack with others of its kind.

A Pokemon that resembles a quadruped wolf. Little things don't shake the calm behavior of Dusk Form Lycanroc, but it carries an intense fighting spirit hidden within, which as a result, it relishes combat at close quarters.

A Pokemon that resembles a rock covered in crystals. Carbink is born from temperatures and pressure underground, and it has slept for millions of years since its birth. Some have been unearthed during cave excavations.

A Pokemon that resembles a sauropod dinosaur or a lizard. The aroma wafting from the leaf-like growths around its neck has a spicy scent, and exhibits various beneficial effects on itself, nearby people, or Pokemon who inhale it.

A Pokemon that resembles a sentient chandelier. Chandelure's fires do not burn its victims physically, instead burning their spirit. After hypnotizing its opponent by waving these flames, it absorbs the victims spirit.
A Pokemon that resembles a shiny, hexagonal snowflake. When its body heat rises it will turn into steam and vanish, but will revert to ice when the body temperature lowers.
A Pokemon that resembles a shrimp. Clawitzer's massive claw can launch cannonballs of water capable of piercing tanker hulls.
A Pokemon that resembles a slouched, bipedal wolf or werewolf. Lycanroc's Midnight Form is thrilled by battling, and becomes more excited the stronger its opponent.
A Pokemon that resembles a small piece of coal. It races around caves in the rough rocky terrain like a unicycle, burning through the red coal that sustains it.

A Pokemon that resembles a small turtle. Rather than actively hunting and foraging for food like most other Pokemon, it collects Berries and stores them in its shell. The Berries inside are liquefied and fermented by Shuckles digestive juices, which it then consumes.
A Pokemon that resembles a snow-covered tree. A curious Pokemon, it often approaches people and can be found inspecting footprints in the snow.
A Pokemon that resembles a spherical tadpole. The direction of the belly spiral differs by area, with the equator being thought to have an effect on this.

A Pokemon that resembles a spider. Rather than making a nest in one specific spot, it wanders in search of food after darkness falls. It will attach silk to its prey and set it free. Later, it tracks the silk to the prey and its friends.
A Pokemon that resembles a sword from the medieval times. The sash is known to suck out the life energy of anyone around whose arm it wraps.

A Pokemon that resembles a tarantula. Galvantula in particular likes to use electrically charged silk to ensnare prey. The electricity stuns the victim, allowing Galvantula to consume the target at its leisure.
A Pokemon that resembles a tumbleweed. Bramblin's main form of locomotion is the wind, which blows it uncontrollably to destinations unknown.
A Pokemon that resembles a turtle. Tirtouga's shell is very tough, and it can dive down to depths of as much as 1000 meters.

A Pokemon that resembles a vaguely anthropomorphic butterfly. Butterfrees wings are covered with poisonous powders that fall off continuously as it flies. This powder repels water, enabling it to gather honey even in the rain.
A Pokemon that resembles a wooly mammoth crossed with a boar. It can endure harsh cold and hunger for an almost indefinite amount of time.

A Pokemon that resembles an over-sized, scorpion. It buries itself in sand and lies in wait for unsuspecting prey, and grips prey with its tail claws, injecting poison; it will then hold on until the poison takes effect.
A Pokemon that resembles four interlocking gears. The red core is used to store energy gained from the rotating gears. This energy can be released through the spiked gear at the bottom.
A Pokemon that resembles three interlocking gears. Klang communicate with each other by spinning their gears in different directions.
A Pokemon that resembles two interlocking gears with six teeth each. Once two bodies have joined, they cannot combine with any others and will rebound without meshing.

A Pokemon that resembles two swords sheathed on a plaque. The swords are able to communicate telepathically, and they use this ability to carry out complex attacks that are unstoppable even to those skilled at swordplay.
A Pokemon which resembles a hand. Binacle always live in pairs on one gray rock, when they fight, one of them will move to a different rock.

A Pokemon which resembles a lizard. Drakloak is capable of flying at speeds greater than 120 mph (193.121 kph). It carries a Dreepy on its head, which it takes care of and fights alongside until the Dreepy manages to evolve.

A Pokemon whose body appears to be constructed out of black crystalline material. Due to the peculiar nature of its body, the power it wields, and the rumors that it came from another world in the distant past, it is speculated that it may be related to the Ultra Beasts if not actually one itself.
A Pokemon with a body closely resembling a living skeleton. It uses its sharp scythes to cut enemies and drink their internal fluids.
A Pokemon with a body of plasma that is shaped like a lightning rod. Rotom has the ability to enter and control appliances and will often pull pranks on unsuspecting people.
A Pokemon with a gaseous body. Haunter hides in very dark places, where it plots to take the life of the next living thing that comes near it.
A Pokemon with a head reminiscent of a helmet. It is a very fast Pokemon; it can attack using ways similar to ninjas.

A Pokemon with a round head and a tiny body. Phione inflates the sac on its head to drift in the water and search for food. When the water grows warm, it will drift in packs with other members of its species.
A Pokemon with a spherical body and a flat, paddle-shaped tail. Fishers detest this troublesome Pokemon because it sprays poison from its spines, getting it everywhere.

A Pokemon with a spherical body and a flat, paddle-shaped tail. In order to attack, Qwilfish drinks over 2.6 gallons (10 litres) of water to inflate its body. It then uses the water pressure to shoot poisonous quills at its foe, which can cause fainting.

A Pokemon with a spherical body. A mysterious life-form having the appearance of a Jigglypuff but with a ferocious aggression that leads it to attack anyone who comes near. Scream Tail is capable of levitating itself, as opposed to walking.
A Pokemon with a sunflower-like design. While the sun is up, it moves around in a hectic manner. When the sun sets, it comes to a complete stop and closes its petals.

A Pokemon with the appearance of a hula dancer. Bellossom is often seen dancing and chanting. In particular, Bellossom dances when cloudy weather persists, or when the heavy rainfall season ends and it is drawn out by the warm sunlight.

A Pokemon with the impression of a stylized rooster. Its known for protecting its home, but it is fickle and will not necessarily help people in need. However, it is very curious, and may come to play or battle with people or Pokemon that interest it.
A Primal form of Groudon. As Primal Groudon, its appearance is similar to Groudon, but larger in size.

A badger like bipedal Pokemon. While combative to the extreme, it doesn't attack often as it prefers taunting an opponent into attacking first. When that happens, it will take a threatening pose posture by crossing its arms and then releasing a staggering voice, so loud and obnoxious that would cause any opponent to flinch.
A badger-like Pokemon with a bulky yet agile body. Typhlosion will make anything go up in flames when angered, and generates shimmering heat from its body when it is ready for battle.
A bagworm-like Pokemon with a coat that has fused with its body. Wormadam that evolve on cold days are said to form thicker cloaks.
A bat-like Pokemon. By alternately resting its front and rear wings, it can fly all day without having to stop.
A bat-like Pokemon. It glides smoothly and silently through the air with its limbs extended, and startles its prey and enemies by flying straight toward them.

A bat-like Pokemon. Noibat is capable of emitting ultrasonic waves of 200,000 Hertz from its ears, which it can use to stun large creatures, immobilize prey, and determine the ripeness of fruit it enjoys eating.

A bat-like Pokemon. When it shakes its tail vigorously, it is producing sound waves powerful enough to destroy concrete. In contrast, it produces waves during courtship that can gladden any who hear it
A bat-like Pokemon. Zubat lives in abundance in caves. It has evolved to have neither eyes nor nostrils, instead navigating through dark environments with echolocation.
A beagle-like, bipedal Pokemon. It has a long tail with an end resembling a paintbrush. This paintbrush oozes with paint, and the color of the paint may vary for each Smeargle.
A bee-like Pokemon. A Vespiquen is far more powerful than its followers, and will only take action if its Combee are unable to protect the hive.
A beetle-like Pokemon that resembles the body of a ladybug. Orbeetle are famous for their large brains and high intelligence. Its large brain is proof of the immense psychic power it possesses.

A beetle-like Pokemon with a large pair of mandibles. It is an adept flier, capable of acrobatic maneuvers such as tailspins and sharp turns. Even as it weaves through complicated tangles of branches in the forest, it is able to maintain high-speed flight.
A bell-shaped Pokemon. Victreebel produces a sweet scent to aid in luring its victims. Acid that has dissolved numerous prey animals becomes sweeter and even more effective at attracting prey.

A bell-shaped Pokemon. Weepinbell camouflages itself as a plant in the forest whilst awaiting an unwary victim. When its prey draws near it sprays toxic pollen to immobilize the target before melting it with its internal acids.
A big, furry Pokemon with an impressive hump on its back. As it is usually unable to see, it checks surroundings with its sensitive pig-like nose instead.
A bipedal Pokemon resembling a chimpanzee. Being very agile, it is able to climb the rocky ledges of tall mountains, where it lives.
A bipedal Pokemon resembling a cross between a mongoose and cat. Zangoose is bitter enemies with Seviper, which it has battled against for many generations.
A bipedal Pokemon resembling a large, portly rabbit. Its ears are strong enough to lift objects weighing over a ton and prove to be an invaluable asset in Diggersby's digging.
A bipedal Pokemon resembling a poison dart frog. By croaking, Toxicroak churns the poison stored in the poison sac on their throat for more potency.
A bipedal Pokemon resembling an ogre. It is known to carry concrete pillars in its massive arms, which it uses to attack strongly without using physical strength or to support its massive upper body.
A bipedal Pokemon similar in appearance to a theropod dinosaur. Its leafy appearance allows it to be camouflaged in the forests where it lives.
A bipedal Pokemon similar to a gremlin. It is feared by people, since it is said to steal a persons soul if they look into its eyes.
A bipedal Pokemon similar to a turtle. Its tail is a popular symbol of longevity, making it popular with the elderly.
A bipedal Pokemon that appears to be a mixture of a pineapple and a duck. Ludicolo becomes more powerful when it hears festive music and will appear near laughing children on hikes.

A bipedal Pokemon that has an ovoid body. Azumarill has highly developed hearing that allows it to hear distances, even when it is underwater. By keeping still and listening closely, it can identity prey even in wild, fast-moving rivers.
A bipedal Pokemon that is similar to a cyclops. Its body is hollow and can absorb anything much like a black hole.

A bipedal Pokemon that resembles a poison dart frog. Croagunks cheek pouches and fingers contain a poisonous fluid. However, the fluid squeezed from its finger is also a significant ingredient in remedies for lower back pain.
A bipedal Pokemon that resembles a pumpkin. The spirit residing in the pumpkin is trapped in this world. Pumpkaboo can carry wandering spirits to where they belong, so they can move on.
A bipedal Pokemon that resembles a tapir. Drowzee is able to put people to sleep, and can then sense the person's dreams. This is so it knows what kind of dream it would be eating.

A bipedal Pokemon that resembles both cats and weasels. Hisuian Sneasel's sturdy and curved claws allow it to climb and travel through the precipitous walls and cliffs where it lives. The venom from the tips of Hisuian Sneasel's claws is capable of invading the nervous system of any prey it scratches.
A bipedal Pokemon that resembles both cats and weasels. Sneasel is a notoriously vicious Pokemon, which is perfectly capable of using its claws to do substantial damage.
A bipedal Pokemon with a Shellder latched onto its head. Galarian Slowking have been observed gathering in groups to chant mysterious spells to use in battle or communicate with each other.

A bipedal Pokemon with a Shellder latched onto its head. Shellder's bite releases venom into Slowpoke's brain, causing a chemical chain-reaction that unlocks a superior intelligence and extraordinary power. More venom is injected into Slowking every time it yawns.
A bipedal Pokemon with a bulky build. Makuhita is very gutsy and never gives up, no matter how many times it is knocked down. Energy is built into its body each time it rises back up.

A bipedal Pokemon with a chubby, vaguely star-shaped body. On the rare occasions it does come down from its mountain home, it can be seen dancing under the light of the full moon. Once the sun starts to rise, it returns home where it sleeps nestled with other Clefairy.

A bipedal Pokemon with a large mouth. Exploud uses the tubes on its body to draw in air and increase its noise-based attacks. Its bellowing is capable of triggering earthquakes and can be heard from over six miles away.

A bipedal Pokemon with a pair of spiky pincers on top of its head. It can use its pincers to crush, toss, bludgeon, or tear opponents, lift things twice its weight, and shatter logs. Captured prey is kept in place by the piercing thorns and sheer strength of Pinsirs horns, and will not be released until they are torn in half.

A bipedal Pokemon with a round body and cactus-like striations. The beauty and fragrance of its flower depend on the harshness of its environment. This flower releases a strong aroma to attract prey. When prey approaches, Cacnea shoots sharp thorns to bring it down.

A bipedal Pokemon with a round body. Primeape is easily angered; even the slightest glance of eye contact will make it furious. When Primeape is furious, its blood circulation is boosted. This makes its muscles stronger, but at the cost of some of its intelligence.

A bipedal Pokemon with a roundish body. Gengar is very mischievous, and at times, malicious. It enjoys playing practical jokes and casting curses, such as pretending to be ones shadow, then behaving erratically. When the quarry notices, the Gengar takes delight in its victims terror.

A bipedal Pokemon with a single green leaf atop its head. Using the leaf on its head as a flute, it makes music with leaves that creates a sense of unease in people. However, it can also play comforting melodies.

A bipedal Pokemon with a spherical body. It is always covered in an oily fluid that allows it to slip away from enemies. All of its skin feels this away except where its swirl is, which is very smooth.

A bipedal Pokemon with a spherical body. Whismur's murmurs are barely audible, but when it senses danger, it lets out an ear-splitting cry. Startled by its own cries, it will cry louder. When it finally stops crying, it will fall asleep from exhaustion.

A bipedal Pokemon with a square build. Loudred is able to shout at high volumes by inhaling, then exhaling using powerful stomach muscles. Additionally, its round ears serve as loudspeakers and it will stomp its feet to build power.
A bipedal Pokemon with an appearance that incorporates features of roses and masquerade attire. Roserade lures prey with a sweet aroma. The more toxic its poison, the sweeter its aroma becomes.
A bipedal Pokemon with an insectoid appearance. Kricketune's melodic cry varies greatly and can be used to signal its emotions.

A bipedal Pokemon with muscular arms. When it swims, it uses all the muscles in its body, and is able to swim vast distances with minimal breathing. It is even capable of briefly running on the waters surface.
A bipedal Pokemon with rudimentary hands and feet. Gloom trickles sticky nectar from its mouth with the appearance and consistency of drool. This can be used as a fertilizer for plants.

A bipedal Pokemon with rudimentary hands and feet. It can shake, flap, or burst its petals into bloom with a bang in order to release clouds of pollen. This pollen is highly allergenic to humans and toxic to other Pokemon; Vileplume uses it to paralyze its prey.

A bipedal Pokemon with straight tusks protruding from the sides of its mouth. These tusks can regenerate if broken, and will regrow if they fall out. This repeated regrowth strengthens and sharpens its tusks.
A bipedal Pokemon. Abra can sense danger by reading minds. When it does, it teleports itself to a safe location so quickly that it creates the illusion of having made copies of itself.

A bipedal Pokemon. Galarian Slowbro are considered highly dangerous due to it indiscriminately attacking its surroundings; the reason for which is due to Shellder sometimes unconsciously biting down hard on its arm.
A bipedal Pokemon. It always carries squared logs and use them to fight with. When it can easily lift a heavy block of timber, it is close to evolving.
A bipedal Pokemon. It has an exceptionally keen sense of smell, being 100 million times that of a human, allowing it to distinguish even the faintest of smells.
A bipedal Pokemon. It is a hyperactive Pokemon. It does not mind walking and running from place to place as it looks for food.
A bipedal Pokemon. It is a master of courtesy and swordsmanship that is capable of predicting its foes moves.
A bipedal Pokemon. It is known to usually carry an I-beam girder in its arms. The steel frame is used to train its muscles, and Gurdurr boasts about its muscles with its comrades.
A bipedal Pokemon. Lickitung's tongue is twice as long as its body. Sticky saliva coats its tongue, which causes a tingling sensation when touched.

A bipedal Pokemon. Magby can breathe 1100 F (600 C) (11068 U) flames, and hot embers drip from its mouth. Its health is determined by these flames. Yellow flames show that a Magby is in good health, while flames mixed with a lot of smoke show that it is fatigued.
A bipedal Pokemon. Marowak is well known for ferocity with its bone club, which it is said to collect from a hidden graveyard.
A bipedal Pokemon. Minun cares more for its teammates than itself, sending off showers of sparks when it cheers for them. When its partner is in trouble, it gives off increasing amounts of sparks.
A bipedal Pokemon. Plusle can create sparkly pom-poms by shorting out the electrical current in its palms. It uses these pom-poms to cheer on its teammates, and will cry loudly if they lose.
A bipedal Pokemon. Slowbro has lost the capability to feel pain due to the Shellder's poison. However, it apparently becomes inspired when the Shellder bites down on its tail.

A bipedal Pokemon. The feelers on its ears act like stethoscopes in that it can feel the beat of another Pokemons heart, to assess the Pokemon's feelings and overall physical condition. The feelers are also able to determine when an Egg is close to hatching.
A bipedal Pokemon. The orb on its tail can shine so bright, that it can be seen from space. People have used the light as a beacon, or to send signals across the ocean.

A bipedal Pokemon. These Pokemon willingly serve people and other Pokemon, as they derive energy from feelings of gratitude. They sense emotions by touching their horns to determine other's needs and serve them better.
A bipedal Pokemon. They are kind but can be relentless when defending territory. They challenge foes with tusks that can cut steel.
A bipedal Pokemon. This Pokemon has even been known to alter unfavorably cold surroundings by spitting scorching flames about to warm up the area and establish an environment more suitable to it.
A bipedal Pokemon. Very mischievous, this Pokemon will tug on fishing lines from underwater and pop out to startle people.

A bipedal automaton Pokemon resembling a suit of armor. Despite its large size, Golurk is capable of flying by inserting its hands in its arms and its legs and feet in its body, then taking off like a rocket.
A bipedal balloon-like Pokemon. This small Pokemon is extremely elastic and can bounce like a ball, although it may not be able to stop if it does this.
A bipedal bulldog-like Pokemon. Despite its fierce appearance, it is actually very timid. Unless Granbull is startled, it will not bite indiscriminately.
A bipedal bulldog-like Pokemon. It is not aggressive and tends to prefer to scare away its opponent rather than fight. However, it is saddened that others run from its frightening appearance.
A bipedal crocodilian Pokemon. Crocalor's internal flame sac has a valve that connects to its vocal cords. As a result, Crocalor lets out guttural cries as it releases fire from its mouth.
A bipedal crocodilian Pokemon. Fuecoco is laid-back and does things at its own pace. It enjoys eating, and it will rush towards any food it sees.
A bipedal feline Pokemon. Perrserker has a violent and barbaric demeanor, and it lives for the thrill of battle.
A bipedal feline Pokemon. The organs hidden in Meowstic's ears emit psychic energy powerful enough to obliterate a 10-ton truck.
A bipedal feline mythical Pokemon. It approaches its enemies at the speed of lightning, then tears them limb from limb with its sharp claws.
A bipedal frog-like Pokemon. Politoed likes to expand its throat and sing. When three or more assemble, they sing in a chorus with a loud, bellowing voice.
A bipedal humanoid Pokemon. Gholdengo is a sociable Pok├⌐mon, able to quickly befriend anybody. It overwhelms opponents by firing coins at them in quick succession.
A bipedal humanoid monkey Pokemon. Thwackey can use its two sticks to create a rhythmic beat. The faster a rhythm Thwackey creates, the more respect it earns from its peers.
A bipedal legendary Pokemon of indefinable but seemingly draconic basis. Black Kyurem is formed by combining with Zekrom and shares many aspects of its design.

A bipedal legendary Pokemon of indefinable but seemingly draconic basis. Kyurem generates a powerful, freezing energy inside itself, but its body became frozen when the energy leaked out. Due to an old legend, it may be assumed Kyurem may be hostile towards Pokemon and humans, due to the fact it supposedly ate them if they were found outside at night.
A bipedal legendary Pokemon of indefinable but seemingly draconic basis. White Kyurem is formed by combining with Reshiram and shares many aspects of its design.

A bipedal legendary Pokemon resembling a dragon or dinosaur. Zekrom's tail consists of large, round, conical and spiked formation, likened to an electricity generator. This tail produces energy for its attacks and emits an anti-gravity field, allowing Zekrom to fly through the air with minimal effects from aerodynamic resistance and gravity.

A bipedal legendary Pokemon with draconic, avian and mammalian traits. Reshiram has a jet engine-like tail, which it uses to accelerate itself when flying at high speeds. It can send flames from its tail into the air to incinerate everything around it.
A bipedal mythical Pokemon. It lurks in the shadows of others, copying their movements and powers.

A bipedal mythical Pokemon. Mew is said to have the DNA of every single Pokemon contained within its body. Since Mew can make itself invisible at will, very few people have knowingly seen it, leading some to declare it extinct and most to assume it to be a mirage.
A bipedal otter-like Pokemon. Scalchop techniques differ from one Dewott to another. It never neglects maintaining its scalchops.
A bipedal sea otter-like Pokemon. It carries a seashell called a "scalchop" on its belly. This shell is made of the same material as its claws, and is used for both battle and cracking hard berries.
A bipedal sheep-like Pokemon. Storing too much electricity caused Flaaffy to lose the wool over most of its body, but the bare, rubbery skin protects it from the electricity stored in its fleece.

A bipedal squirrel-like Pokemon. True to their name, Greedent are extremely greedy and gluttonous. Greedent stuff their tails with so many Berries, that these berries fall out constantly, especially when it is hit or faints.
A bipedal ursine Pokemon. The marking on its face glows when it finds honey already made. Honey is often absorbed into the forepaws, and Teddiursa is often seen licking them.

A bipedal ursine Pokemon. While it is skilled at climbing trees, it gathers food by snapping them and collecting whatever berries or fruits fall down. It will mark trees bearing delicious fruit in its territory with its claws.

A bipedal weasel-like Pokemon. Due to its severe poison and deadly physical power, no other Pokemon species can defeat Sneasler in its habitat. Using its claws, Sneasler is capable of climbing up walls and cliffs with ease.
A bipedal, amphibious Pokemon, somewhat resembling a mantis shrimp. Its strong claws can break stones and punch through a steel slab. Furthermore, they can be freely extended or retracted.
A bipedal, amphibious Pokemon. An unintelligent Pokemon, it tends to bump its head inadvertently while swimming and seems not to care.
A bipedal, anteater-like Pokemon. Durant are the preferred prey of Heatmor. It burns through Durant's steel bodies with its tongue and consumes their insides.

A bipedal, ape-like Pokemon. Rillaboom always carries its signature drum with it on its back, and pulls it out when engaged in battle. By drumming, Rillaboom can tap into the power of its special tree stump.
A bipedal, beetle-like Pokemon. Using its horn, it throws opponents or competitors for food. It can lift and throw objects 100 times its own weight.
A bipedal, bird-like legendary Pokemon. Tornadus can travel at speeds of 200 miles per hour (320 kilometers per hour). It can also whip up storms with its tail, and is able to blow away houses.

A bipedal, bovine Pokemon. The milk that it produces is sweet and very nutritious, and can be used to heal Pokemon and ill or weary humans. It can produce over five gallons of milk per day, which in turn can be turned into yogurt or enjoyed unchanged by children and adults alike.
A bipedal, bug-like Pokemon. By shaking its head and rubbing its antennae together, it is able to create a xylophonic sound that it uses to communicate.
A bipedal, canine-like Pokemon. Lucario is considered to be prideful, and is extremely loyal to its Trainer. It also seems to have a natural sense of justice.
A bipedal, chicken-like Pokemon. Its flames burn more intensely when it faces stronger opponents. Every several years, its old feathers burn off, and new, supple feathers grow back in their place.
A bipedal, chicken-like Pokemon. While it is fighting, it is noisy and produces sharp cries that distract and intimidate its opponent.
A bipedal, clay Pokemon. Golett burns energy inside itself in order to move. This energy causes Golett to release light through the holes near its arms and legs.
A bipedal, draconian Pokemon. Garchomp can fly at an incredible speed, helped by the fine scales on its body that reduce drag to catch its prey.
A bipedal, draconic Pokemon. Fights over turf often break out between it and another Fraxure. After a fight, it sharpen its tusks on river rocks, as they do not regenerate.

A bipedal, duck-like Pokemon. Golduck is a fast swimmer, out-swimming even the most athletic of humans because of its webbed hands and feet. Even rough seas do not hamper this Pokemon's swimming abilities, and it will sometimes rescue people from shipwrecks.
A bipedal, feline Pokemon with a muscular build. Incineroar's flame belt is produced from within its body and burst from its navel and waist as its fighting spirit rises.
A bipedal, feline Pokemon. Floragato is intelligent and dexterous. It is also mischievous and likes showing off, desiring attention and companionship from others.

A bipedal, fox-like Pokemon. As a result of its apearance, Hisuian Zoroark was said to resemble an embodiment of death. The illusions channeled through Hisuian Zoroark's long withering fur are full of spite. Uniquely, this spiteful illusion can cause physical harm to its opponent on both the inside and outside.
A bipedal, fox-like Pokemon. Braixen always keeps a stick in its tail, which it sets alight using its bushy tail fur. The flame from the lit twig is used for both attack and communication.

A bipedal, fox-like Pokemon. Zoroark can create illusions that are indistinguishable from reality, deluding many people simultaneously. It is extremely protective of those it cares about and will go to any lengths to keep them safe, including risking its own life, and it can hold grudges on those who harm its loved ones.
A bipedal, frog-like Pokemon. Frogadier is a nimble and swift Pokemon; it can scale a tower exceeding 2,000 feet in one minute, and it can throw bubble-coated pebbles at targets up to 100 feet away.
A bipedal, ground dwelling pholidote Pokemon. Despite the weight of its ice-covered body, Alolan Sandslash is able to move swiftly by carving a path in the snow with its claws.
A bipedal, ground dwelling pholidote Pokemon. Its claws and spikes can both break off and are shed regularly, but grow back quickly.
A bipedal, ground dwelling pholidote Pokemon. Sandshrew can quickly curl into a tight ball to protect itself from great falls and opponents, but may also throw sand at attackers.
A bipedal, ground dwelling pholidote Pokemon. The steel-like covering grants it extra defense, but it is unable to curl into a ball like its desert counterpart.

A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon that appears to be wearing a tutu. Kirlia's horns are used to amplify its psychokinetic power and distort the air around it. The distortion in the air causes scenery mirages and can cause a rip in dimensions.
A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon that resembles a woman. It prefers to communicate by using dance-like movements. These rhythmic movements often cause people to dance along with it.

A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon whose body resembles a flowing gown. Gardevoir is able to see the future using its psychic powers. Additionally, it is able to create small black holes, distort dimensions, and support itself without feeling the pull of gravity.
A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon with four well-muscled arms. Machamp punches extremely fast, throwing five hundred punches a second. With only one hand, it can move a mountain.

A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon. Armarouge is loyal and believes in fighting fair, willing to fight head-on no matter how strong the foe is. It first focuses on using its sturdy armor for defense before using high firepower in order to take down opponents.
A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon. Bisharp rules over a pack of Pawniard, and fights other Bisharp to become the alpha of the pack. The loser of these fights is cast out.
A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon. Ceruledge is merciless and will do anything to win a battle. It prefers to do close-quarters combat, with a mix of sneak and surprise attacks.

A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon. From birth, this Pokemon is an excellent pantomime. As it matures, it gains the ability to solidify air molecules by vibrating its fingertips. This ability allows it to create invisible objects with its gestures.
A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon. If anyone comes by Hypno, it will hypnotize them and eat their dreams. While it awaits its prey, it polishes its pendulum.
A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon. It is driven to throw larger opponents and will always try to do so.

A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon. Machoke is a Pokemon of immense strength. Its muscles are as hard as steel, and it is capable of lifting extremely heavy objects with only one finger. In spite of this, it is modest and often helps people with manual labor.
A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon. Mr. Rime is highly skilled in tap dancing and waves its ice cane while it moves gracefully. It can release psychic powers through the pattern on its belly.
A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon. Sawk is found secluded in the mountains where it trains to increase its strength. It becomes angered if it is interrupted while training.
A bipedal, humanoid Pokemon. Through its feet, it is able to control the temperature and create a floor of ice, which it can kick up to act as a barrier.
A bipedal, humanoid legendary Pokemon with some feline features. It is said to have the most savage heart among all Pokemon, lack compassion, and strike fear into its enemy with cold, glowing eyes.
A bipedal, insectoid Pokemon with a metallic exoskeleton. It will raise its claws and wave them around to scare off predators or foes, giving it the appearance of having three heads.

A bipedal, insectoid Pokemon. Scyther's blade-like forearms are capable of slicing through logs, and become sharper by cutting through hard materials. Using swift movements, it camouflages itself and enhances the effectiveness of its scythes.
A bipedal, insectoid mythical Pokemon. The powerful cannon on its back and other enhancements were apparently added as part of the bizarre modifications made to it.
A bipedal, lizard-like Pokemon. Amped Form Toxtricity are known to be short-tempered and extremely confident. This form aggressively attacks anything that makes eye contact with it.

A bipedal, lizard-like Pokemon. Low Key Form Toxtricity are known to be selfish and have a high regard towards its strength. Unlike its Amped form counterpart, Toxtricity prefers to taunt opponents into fighting it when making eye contact with them.
A bipedal, lizard-like Pokemon. Scrafty is powerful enough to kick through concrete blocks, and can also spit acidic liquid from its mouth.
A bipedal, lizard-like Pokemon. Scraggy is easily engaged in battle, as it will attack any foe that so much as meets its gaze with its thick cranium.
A bipedal, mammalian Pokemon with some plant-like features. Once it gets into its defensive stance with its hands covering its face, it can stand up to a bombs explosion.
A bipedal, mammalian Pokemon with some plant-like features. When it is forced to defend itself, it relies on its shell to deflect attacks, before counterattacking with its sharp quills.
A bipedal, mammalian Pokemon. Despite having a curious nature that tends to get it in trouble, Chespin keeps an optimistic outlook and does not worry about small details.

A bipedal, mushroom-like Pokemon with some kangaroo-like qualities. Breloom can stretch its short arms to deliver fast punches. Additionally, it has light, springy footwork that allows it to get close to opponents.
A bipedal, mustelid-like Pokemon. In fights, they dominate with onslaughts of flowing, continuous attacks. It takes pride in the speed at which it can use moves.
A bipedal, panda Pokemon with rabbit-like features. It has dizzying, confusing, and scattering dance-like movements. These movements confuse its opponents and make it difficult for them to aim at it.
A bipedal, pig-like Pokemon. Pignite has a fire in its stomach, which it fuels with food. The intensity of this flame increases as fuel is added or when Pignite is angered.
A bipedal, pig-like Pokemon. There appear to be three shining pearls on its body. These pearls are used to amplify its psychic powers, which allow it to control its opponents.

A bipedal, plant-like Pokemon with a humanoid appearance. This Pokemon has a high-class nature, and punishes anyone that approaches it with evil in mind. This attitude will even be directed at its Trainer if given commands Tsareena dislikes, such as being told to use an ineffective move.
A bipedal, plant-like Pokemon with a humanoid appearance. While it has a delectable fragrance, this Pokemon also has a tomboyish personality that can make it hard to get along with.
A bipedal, primate-like Pokemon. The flame on Monferno's tail has several purposes. It can be controlled to keep opponents at an ideal distance or stretched in order to make Monferno appear larger.
A bipedal, primate-like Pokemon. This quick Pokemon practices a unique kind of martial art that involves all of its limbs. This style uses fiery punches and kicks as well.

A bipedal, pumpkin Pokemon. Gourgeist are malevolent Pokemon that catch their prey in their hairlike arms and take delight in their victim's suffering. On moonless nights, they are known to wander through town streets, singing an eerie song that curses its unfortunate listeners.

A bipedal, rabbit-like Pokemon. Due to its strong core and great balance, Cinderace can unleash powerful kicks from any position. In battle, it uses artful footwork to feint and throw its opponents off.
A bipedal, rabbit-like Pokemon. Lopunny is a timid Pokemon that will cloak its body with its ears or spring away when it senses danger.

A bipedal, reptilian Pokemon covered in scaly armor. Because it does not wish to fight weak foes, it clangs its scales together when it senses someone approaching. This ringing sound alerts others of its presence. The power of this Pokemon's uppercut is enough to send foes flying.

A bipedal, reptilian Pokemon that resembles a chameleon. Inteleon has many hidden capabilities. It has a long, extendable yellow membrane on its back that allows it to glide in the air and nictitating membranes that allow it to analyze for an opponent's weak point.

A bipedal, reptilian Pokemon vaguely resembling Pachycephalosaurus. It longs to fly and dreams of one day being able to do so. Frustrated at its inability to fly, it leaps off cliffs and smashes its head against large rocks. This process of continually bashing its head causes it to become as hard as steel.

A bipedal, reptilian Pokemon with a slender build. Its tail is capable of performing photosynthesis, which allows Snivy to move more quickly. However, the tail will begin to droop when Snivy loses energy.

A bipedal, reptilian Pokemon with many scaly plates. When it finds an opponent, it dances and clangs its scales together to show its strength. This ferocious dance climaxes with a challenging war cry.
A bipedal, reptilian Pokemon. A fire burns at the tip of this Pokemon's slender tail, and is said that Charmander dies if its flame goes out.

A bipedal, reptilian Pokemon. Charmeleon has a vicious nature and will constantly seek out opponents. Strong opponents excite this Pokemon, causing it to spout bluish-white flames that torch its surroundings.
A bipedal, reptilian Pokemon. Kecleon is able to change the colors of its body at will, and is known for frequently using this ability to camouflage itself.

A bipedal, rodent-like Pokemon. By collecting its psychic power in its tail, it is able to ride it like a surfboard and float in the air. While its cheek sacs are still used to store electricity, rubbing them releases a sweet aroma.

A bipedal, rodent-like Pokemon. Raichu exudes a weak electrical charge from all its body and slightly glows in the dark, and is capable of storing over 100,000 volts of electricity. However, it will become aggressive if it has stored too much electricity.
A bipedal, rosebud-like Pokemon. It keeps its buds closed during the cold winter, but opens them again in the spring and releases pollen.

A bipedal, turtle-like Pokemon with a spiny shell. When prey steps onto its shell, it strikes itself with its own tail to cause an explosion. The explosion is ignited by sparks from the spikes on its shell, and released through the hole on its chest.

A bipedal, ursine Pokemon. Cubchoo's nose is constantly running. It inhales the mucus and uses it in its attacks. If it is in bad health, the mucus becomes watery, which weakens its Ice-type techniques.
A bipedal, weasel-like Pokemon. Weavile is devious and intelligent. It usually lives in cold, icy areas where it forms small packs. Using teamwork to take down its prey.

A bipedial legendary Pokemon. It has been referred to as the "King of Bountiful Harvests" due to its role in bringing lush vegetation and harvests yearly. Calyrex's right hand can cause the land to be covered in verdant grass and blooms. The left hand of Calyrex allows it to make the fields of fruit become ripen and heavy.
A bird-like, legendary Pokemon with an aerodynamic body. Its body can refract light, which allows it to become invisible or alter its appearance.

A blob-like Pokemon with a geometric shaped shell. While growing inside, Dottler uses its shell to examine its environment, using its psychic powers to keep itself protected and gather information about its habitat until it evolves.
A boulder Pokemon with arms. It is often stepped on, and will sometimes swing its arms in anger when this occurs.
A boulder Pokemon with arms. There are areas on the Alolan Geodude's body that are especially magnetic and attracts iron sand.
A bovine, quadruped legendary Pokemon. It is strong enough to destroy a castle wall in one blow.

A bulky quadruped Pokemon resembling a tortoise. Torterra's large and clean shell supports the lives of many small Pokemon, which occasionally gather and build their nests upon the shell. Some are born and spend their entire life there.
A bulky, bipedal Pokemon similar to a beaver. This Pokemon is known to be an industrious worker that dams rivers by building its nest.
A bulky, bipedal Pokemon with pig-like features. Using the wreath of flames on its neck and shoulders, Emboar will set its hands on fire.
A bulky, bipedal canine legendary Pokemon. Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.
A bulky, bipedal crocodilian Pokemon. When hunting or fighting, Feraligatr is agile and fast, due to its powerful hind legs that are used to kick the ground hard and charge.

A bulky, bipedal toad-like Pokemon. The various lumps on its body have varying capabilities. The ones on its head can shoot a paralyzing liquid, while the ones on its hands can be vibrated to increase its punching power.

A butterfly-like Pokemon with wings that come in a large variety of patterns. Its wing's pattern is affected by the climate in which it lives and can spread its scales to calm an opponents fighting spirit.

A butterfly-like Pokemon. Beautifly has long and curled proboscis that it uses to drain body fluids from its prey. Additionally, this aggressive Pokemon will jab at foes with its proboscis if it is disturbed while collecting pollen.

A cactus-like Pokemon, with large ear-like extensions. When Maractus moves its body rhythmically, it emits sounds reminiscent of maracas being played. This allows Maractus to produce up-tempo songs and dances that it can use to scare away predators.
A canine Pokemon with a talent for rescuing people lost at sea or in the mountains. Its fur is thick enough to protect itself and others against freezing temperatures.
A canine Pokemon. Herdier is very loyal, and it will help its Trainer raise other Pokemon.
A canine Pokemon. It is an intelligent, courageous Pokemon capable of judging its opponents strength.
A canine Pokemon. It uses friction from the atmosphere to generate electricity. Because of this, its body gives off showers of sparks in seasons with arid air or before a storm.

A canine, quadruped Pokemon. Manectric gathers electricity in its mane and then discharges it. This process creates thunderclouds, which it uses in battle. Since lightning falls in its vicinity, it is said to have been born from lightning and make its nest where lightning has struck.
A caterpillar-like Pokemon. Sewaddle makes itself leafy clothes using chewed-up leaves and a thread-like substance it produces from its mouth.
A catfish-like Pokemon. It causes earthquakes that can extend for over three miles, and can predict when natural earthquakes will occur.

A centipede-like Pokemon. It is very aggressive and will not give up until victorious. This Pokemon chases down enemies with great speed, and then attacks relentlessly with its horns until it prevails.
A cephalopod-like Pokemon. In the wild, it will spurt ink at predators to protect its young from danger.
A cetacean Pokemon resembling a dolphin. It likes playing with others of its kind using the water ring on its tail. It uses ultrasonic waves to sense the emotions of other living creatures.
A cetacean Pokemon resembling a dolphin. Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen's, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up.

A cetacean Pokemon resembling a dolphin. Palafin is known as the "Pelagic Protector". When it hears its allies calling for help, Palafin will change its appearance from its Zero Form to its Hero Form.

A chimp-like Pokemon. It uses its stick to beat rhythmically against the surfaces of all sorts of objects. This has been observed to cause grass to grow, and wilted flowers and leaves seem to regain their color when Grookey drums nearby.

A chubby, spherical, seal-like Pokemon. When happy or cheerful, such as when eating in a group, this Pokemon will clap its fins. Because its body is poorly shaped for swimming and can only walk slowly, it moves primarily by rolling across ice floes.

A circular Pokemon. Cottonee is blown around by the wind because of its lightweight composition. The only circumstance in which it cannot be blown by wind is when it has been soaked by rain, which weighs it down and makes it soggy.
A cocoon Pokemon. When it comes close to evolving, its body gives off heat that makes it warm to the touch.

A cocoon-like Pokemon. It is almost completely covered in silk which forms a hard cocoon that it can use to repel enemy attacks. Dew and rainwater collect on the silk, which provides Silcoon with nourishment.

A cocoon-like Pokemon. It is covered in silk which hardens into a tough cocoon that is able to endure attacks, and this Pokemon will not move even when it is attacked. However, it never forgets the pain it endures and seek revenge upon evolution.

A composite Pokemon sharing physical traits of aquatic and land animals. It has a cell composition similar to water molecules. This structure allows Vaporeon to melt into water at will and keeps it camouflaged as it swims.
A condor-like Pokemon. One theory explains that Xatu can see into the future with its right eye and the past with its left, and it does not move due to fears of its visions of the future coming true.
A coned flower Pokemon. It can latch onto walls to disguise itself as a plant. Should Glimmora sense danger, it will open all its petals to unleash a beam attack in retaliation.
A coral-like Pokemon with an ectoplasmic "body". This ectoplasm was a result of a long and continuous process absorbing spirit energy from other creatures. Anyone who touches it will rapidly stiffen.
A crocodilian Pokemon. Skeledirge has a meddlesome but caring personality. Its singing is gentle, but powerful and full of vitality, capable of soothing the souls of all who hears it.
A cross between a Zuniceratops and a bulldozer. If a herd of Bastiodon is attacked, the adults will line up in a wall around their young. Their rock-hard heads can repulse any attack.
A crow-like, avian Pokemon. Corvisquire are intelligent enough to use tools in battle, having been seen to throw rocks at their opponents or use vines to entangle them.
A crustacean Pokemon resembling a crab. A competitive Pokemon that hates to lose, Crabrawler strives to achieve not only a high social standing, but a physically higher position as well.
A crustacean Pokemon resembling a crab. While Kingler's large, left claw is it main tool for offensive maneuvers, it is so large and heavy that Kingler can barely lift it.

A crustacean Pokemon resembling both a horsehair crab and the mythical yeti. It just throws punches indiscriminately. In times of desperation, it can lop off its own pincers and fire them like rockets.
A crustacean Pokemon similar to a crab. In times of scarce food sources, it may eat sand to regain nutrients, and will be very aggressive in defending its home.
A crustacean Pokemon. A hardy creature, Corphish is able to live in polluted water and eat nearly anything.
A crustacean Pokemon. Because of its constant challenges to battle, no other Pokemon wants to inhabit its territory. Any that do venture too close are tossed out of its pond with its pincers.
A crustacean Pokemon. Clauncher uses its larger claw to shoot compressed water like a pistol shot at its prey. Up close, the compressed water can shatter rocks.

A crustacean Pokemon. Klawf hangs upside-down from the sheer cliffs on which it lives in order to ambush its prey from above; however, it can't stay in this position for too long as its blood will rush to its head, causing it to get dizzy.
A crystal plant-like Pokemon. Glimmet's diet consists of absorbing minerals from the walls of caves. To defend itself from foes, Glimmet scatters poisonous powder from its petals.

A dainty bipedal Pokemon that is small in stature. Togetic can sense the kindness in other people and Pokemon's hearts. Whenever it spots a pure-hearted person, it tends to go to that person and shower them with happiness and glowing down called "joy dust".
A deer-like Pokemon. Sawsbuck lives in herds led by the Sawsbuck with the most splendid antlers. It can live almost anywhere as they adapt to the season.
A dinosaur-like Pokemon resembling the Pachycephalosaurus. When it lived in dense forests and jungles 100 million years ago, it would use headbutts to snap obstructing trees and down its prey.

A dinosaurian Pokemon, closely resembling theropods such as Tyrannosaurus. Tyrunt will throw tantrums and run wild if it encounters something it does not like, and its strong jaws have enough force to shred an automobile.
A dog-like Pokemon similar to a poodle. This Pokemon's furry coat cushions it against physical attacks. Some domesticated Furfrou are commonly seen with their fur trimmed into various styles.

A doll-like Pokemon that is possessed by pure hatred. Being driven to life by a powerful grudge, it keeps its life force safely in its body by the means of its zipped up mouth. If unzipped, it would lose its energy.

A draconic Pokemon. Dragapult carries a pair of Dreepy inside its horns, which it will fire at its opponents like supersonic missiles during battle. It's said that the Dreepy it carries greatly enjoy being sent flying toward opponents at immense speeds.

A draconic, bipedal Pokemon. Despite its bulky build, Dragonite is capable of flying faster than the speed of sound. It can circle the globe in sixteen hours, traveling roughly 1,556 mph (2,505 km/h), or about three times the speed of an average airplane.

A draconic, bipedal Pokemon. This Pokemon flies in search of powerful opponents to battle, and its fire will burn hotter as it gains experience. Its fiery breath is capable of melting boulders, massive glaciers, and has been known to accidentally cause forest fires.
A dragon-like Pokemon inhabiting a body reminiscent of apple pie. Appletun produces a nectar-like scent which attracts Bug-type Pokemon, which it preys on. The skin on its back is especially yummy.
A dragonfly-like Pokemon. Vibrava's wings are not fully developed, so it is unable to fly very far. However, it is able to create vibrations and ultrasonic waves with its wings.
A duck-like Pokemon. Quaxwell has a serious, stoic personality. It learns and practices dance routines by observing the movements of people and Pokemon from various regions.
A duckling-like Pokemon. It is a talented diver and can spray water from its feathers for self-defense. The foe is distracted by the spray, allowing Ducklett to escape.
A duckling-like Pokemon. Quaxly is an earnest and tidy Pokemon, and tends to overthink things. It hates getting itself dirty, especially on its head.
A electric golem-like legendary Pokemon. Regieleki absorbs electrons in order to stay alive and is said to have the greatest power of any Electric-type Pokemon.
A fairy-like mythical Pokemon. It is able to travel through time and exist simultaneously throughout time, and plant life flourishes wherever it has been.
A fawn-like Pokemon, most resembling a fallow deer. It can change in appearance with the changing of the seasons. If it senses animosity, it hides in tall grass.

A feline Pokemon with a slender physique. Glameow tends to be spiteful and fickle, having a tendency to hook its claws into the nose of its owner if its not fed. When its happy, it demonstrates movements with its tail, like a dancing ribbon.
A feline Pokemon. It is fascinated by moving objects, and chases them. It is known to chase its own tail and become dizzy from it.
A feline Pokemon. Purrloin is a mischievous Pokemon that likes to steal from people. It will put on a cute act in order to get its victims to let its guard down.
A feline legendary Pokemon. Chien-Pao is able to control 100 tons of fallen snow, causing avalanches and playing around in them innocently.
A feline, quadruped Pokemon resembling a young lynx or lion. Luxio is able to communicate with others of its kind using electrical pulses from its claws.
A femininely anthropomorphic mythical Pokemon. Meloetta's beautiful music and dance inspired many works of art, music, and songs. This made the Pokemon popular among both musicians and dancers.

A firefly-like, bipedal Pokemon. Illumise uses its sweet aromas to lure in Volbeat and have them draw geometric patterns in the sky. It is said to earn respect from others by composing designs that are more complex.
A firefly-like, bipedal Pokemon. It has a spherical yellow tail, which glows to communicate and draw geometric patterns in the sky while in a swarm.
A fish Pokemon with a body covered in tiny, sharp denticles. It swarms any intruder and prey that invade its territory, and becomes timid when it is alone.
A fish Pokemon. Both forms of Basculin are extremely hostile, especially towards their opposite form. Red and blue striped Basculin generally start fighting each other on sight.

A fish-like Pokemon covered in colorful scales and fins. This Pokemon buries itself on the seafloor, leaving only the growth on its head exposed. By emitting a low level of psychic power, it serves as radar to detect prey.

A fish-like Pokemon with a heart-shaped body. If it finds an injured Pokemon floating at sea, Alomomola will heal the Pokemon's wounds and carry it back to shore. It heals Pokemon using its special membrane enveloping its entire body.
A fish-like Pokemon with a relatively flat body in the shape of a heart. Loving couples gave this Pokemon its name after spotting it in the ocean waters.
